title: Lisbon Piri-Piri Linguica Spread
seoTitle: Lisbon Piri-Piri Linguica Spread | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Linguica grill platter—smoked pork sausage, pepper heat, hall family-style
subtitle: Smoked sausage, piri-piri onions, and grilled peppers for ten
description: Portuguese linguica grills until split and charred, served on platters with piri-piri grilled onions, roasted peppers, and crusty rolls.

steps.title: Prep linguica
steps.instruction: Score linguica links lightly lengthwise—helps render fat and char. Bring to room temp 20 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season onions and peppers
steps.instruction: Toss onion rings and pepper quarters with olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika, and salt. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium, 400°F. Have cooler zone ready for sausage fat flare-ups. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill linguica
steps.instruction: Grill sausage links 12–15 minutes, turning often, until split, charred, and 160°F internal. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill veg
steps.instruction: Grill onions and peppers alongside sausage until charred and tender, 10–12 minutes. Brush onions with piri-piri halfway. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Rest sausage 5 minutes. Slice on bias into 1-inch pieces. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Pile sliced linguica and veg into hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F until service. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Platter for ten
steps.instruction: Family-style platters with sausage, peppers, onions, rolls, and mustard. About 10 oz sausage per firefighter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Score links lightly—deep cuts cause linguica to split open and dry out.
Piri-piri on onions at the line, not during long hold.
Sliced on bias looks better on platters and catches more char.
tonightSpread: Linguica platter with piri-piri onions and grilled peppers.
Simple potato salad or greens on the side.
leftovers: Linguica slices into breakfast hash with eggs.
Chop into tomato stew with paprika.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Linguica is a one-pan protein win—smoked sausage grills fast, holds at 170°F, and feeds ten without a smoker. Different from generic sausage-pepper trays.
mealPrepNotes: Score sausage lightly. Grill medium 400°F, 12–15 minutes turning often. Hold sliced sausage covered at 170°F up to 45 minutes. Onions grill alongside.
